dimensions.evidence: The tabs (Code, Issues 4, Pull Requests, Actions…) follow GitHub/GitLab conventions, as do the Watch/Star/Fork buttons with counters and the folder/file icons. The README header has an 'Escape' button next to the edit pencil.
dimensions.justification: Components, icons and counter badges are used consistently and match Git platform conventions. The 'Escape' button is not a standard control on README panels, and its bordered-text style differs from the icon-only edit button next to it.

dimensions.evidence: The 'Code' tab is active (bold with an underline). The branch selector shows 'main'. The latest commit shows hash 3708f923a3, message 'Add docs/INSTALL.md' and 'now'. Counters: 3 Commits, 1 Branch, 0 Tags, Issues 4, Watching 1.
dimensions.justification: Location and repository state are clearly shown. Every timestamp reads 'now', which does not separate the commits from each other. A relative time with an absolute date (e.g. on hover) cannot be confirmed from the screenshot.

dimensions.evidence: Labels such as 'Go to file', 'Add File', '3 Commits', 'Manage Topics' and 'Search code...' are clear. The 'Escape' button in the README header has no visible explanation.
dimensions.justification: Most labels are short and clear. 'Escape' is jargon: it is unclear whether it escapes Unicode characters or closes something, and users may avoid it or click it by mistake.

dimensions.evidence: The page has mostly read-only content. Settings sits separately on the far right of the tab bar. 'Add File' and the edit pencil open separate flows. The unlabeled icon button next to the branch selector (compare/PR) has no text.
dimensions.justification: There are few chances to make an error on this view, and destructive settings are kept apart. Icon-only buttons (the compare icon next to 'main', the RSS icon) could lead to accidental navigation. The impact is low.

dimensions.evidence: The 'docs' folder appears directly in the list, and its last-commit message 'Add docs/INSTALL.md' names the file. 'Go to file' has a T shortcut hint and 'Search code...' has an S hint. The latest commit hash is shown at the top of the list and can be clicked.
dimensions.justification: The task takes one or two clicks: open docs and then INSTALL.md, or use Go to file. The latest commit is visible right away. Keyboard shortcut hints support recognition over recall.

dimensions.evidence: The sidebar lists Readme, 26 KiB, 0 Stars, 1 Watchers, 0 Forks and a Languages bar. The header has Watch, Star and Fork counters plus an RSS button. The footer shows 'Page: 13ms Template: 3ms'.
dimensions.justification: The design is clean overall. Some information is repeated: star, watcher and fork counts appear in both the header buttons and the sidebar. The page render timings in the footer are developer noise for end users.

dimensions.evidence: Dark theme. Commit messages in the file list ('Add docs/INSTALL.md', 'Initial commit') and the 'now' timestamps are mid-grey on near-black. Counter badges ('4', '1', '0') are small grey-on-grey. Control borders (Go to file, branch selector) are low-contrast dark grey. The compare and RSS icon buttons have no text labels.
dimensions.justification: Main text is readable, but secondary text, badges and input/button borders appear to be near the minimum contrast thresholds (WCAG 1.4.3 / 1.4.11). Small counter badges and icon-only buttons make the page harder to use for low-vision users. Focus indicators cannot be assessed from a static screenshot.

strengths: The file list shows each item's last commit message, and the latest commit (hash, author, message) sits right above it. This makes the typical task fast.
The repository navigation follows familiar Git platform conventions: an active Code tab, counters, a branch selector, and Watch/Star/Fork buttons.
'Go to file' (T) and 'Search code' (S) show visible keyboard shortcut hints, which speeds up navigation.

recommendations.recommendation: Increase contrast for secondary text (commit messages, timestamps), counter badges and control borders in the dark theme to at least 4.5:1 for text and 3:1 for UI component boundaries.
Replace the bare 'Escape' button in the README header with a descriptive label or tooltip (e.g. 'Show escaped characters'), or hide it unless ambiguous characters are actually present.
Add visible text labels or tooltips and aria-labels to the icon-only buttons (the compare icon next to the branch selector, RSS, the README edit pencil).
Visually set the latest-commit row apart from the file rows (e.g. a 'Latest commit' label or a tinted background), and show absolute dates alongside relative times like 'now'.
Remove the star, watcher and fork counts that duplicate the header buttons from the sidebar, and hide the page/template render timings from regular users.

dimensions.evidence: The repo title 'judge-demo / web-shop' sits top-left, with the tab bar (Code active) below it. The commit message column is placed far from the file names (starting around x=457), which leaves a wide gap that weakens the visual link between a row's name and its message. Spacing is otherwise even.

dimensions.evidence: The tabs (Code, Issues, Pull Requests, Actions, ...), the Watch/Star/Fork buttons with counters, the branch selector 'main', 'Go to file' with a T shortcut, and the green 'Code' clone button follow GitHub/GitLab conventions. Icons are used the same way across tabs and sidebar items.
dimensions.justification: The page matches Git platform standards closely. One small inconsistency: the README header has a text button 'Escape' next to an icon-only pencil edit button, so the same header mixes two action styles. The commit-to-branch compare button next to 'main' is icon-only, while similar toolbar actions have text labels.

dimensions.evidence: The 'Code' tab is underlined and bold. The breadcrumb shows 'judge-demo / web-shop'. Counters are visible: '3 Commits', '1 Branch', '0 Tags', Issues '4', Watching '1', Star '0', Fork '0'. The latest commit bar shows the hash 3708f923a3 and 'now'.
dimensions.justification: Location and repository state are clear. Timestamps use only the relative value 'now', with no absolute date shown. That is fine for a fresh repo but gives little precision when you check the latest commit.

dimensions.evidence: The README header has a button labelled 'Escape'. Other labels are plain: 'Go to file', 'Add File', 'Manage Topics', 'Watching'. The sidebar shows '26 KiB'.
dimensions.justification: Most labels are clear. 'Escape' is jargon (it escapes ambiguous Unicode characters), and its meaning isn't obvious on a simple README. Users could mistake it for a close or cancel action. Fix: rename it to something like 'Show escaped characters', or add a tooltip or warning text that explains why it appears.

dimensions.evidence: No destructive actions are exposed in the main area. 'Settings' is set apart on the far right of the tab bar. 'Add File' and 'Code' are dropdowns, so a click doesn't immediately commit to an action.
dimensions.justification: This view is read-only, so there is little risk of error. Settings is separated from the content tabs. Confirmation behaviour can't be assessed from the screenshot. The ambiguous 'Escape' toggle could cause brief confusion but is harmless.

dimensions.evidence: The 'docs' folder is in the file list, and its last commit message 'Add docs/INSTALL.md' is shown inline. The latest commit bar at the top shows 'Add docs/INSTALL.md' with a clickable hash. 'Go to file' has a T keyboard shortcut, and 'Search code...' has an S shortcut.
dimensions.justification: The task takes very few steps. The latest commit is visible right away, and docs/INSTALL.md is one click away through 'docs' or the 'Go to file' search. The keyboard shortcuts are shown visibly, which supports recognition over recall.

dimensions.evidence: The page is compact and uncluttered. The sidebar has Description, Manage Topics, Readme, 26 KiB, 0 Stars, 1 Watchers, 0 Forks and Languages. The Stars, Watchers and Forks counts repeat the header buttons Star 0, Fork 0 and Watching 1. The footer shows 'Page: 13ms Template: 3ms'.
dimensions.justification: Density suits the task. There is a little redundancy: social counts appear both in the header and in the sidebar, and the footer shows render timing, which is developer-facing noise.

dimensions.evidence: Secondary grey text on the dark background is low contrast: commit messages 'Add src/app.py' and 'Initial commit', 'now' timestamps, the 'Manage Topics' label, and the 'Go to file' and 'Search code...' placeholders. Control borders such as the 'Escape' button and toolbar buttons are very faint. Small keyboard-hint badges read 'T' and 'S'. The README.md icon (blue info circle) differs from the folder icons by colour and shape.
dimensions.justification: Primary text is legible and most targets look like they are 24px or larger. Several grey-on-dark texts and thin borders look borderline for WCAG 1.4.3 (4.5:1 text contrast) and 1.4.11 (3:1 for control boundaries). Fix: lighten the secondary text colour and increase the contrast of control borders in the dark theme. Focus visibility (2.4.7) can't be assessed from a static screenshot.

strengths: The latest commit (author, hash, message, time) is shown prominently right above the file list, so checking it takes no extra clicks.
Navigation follows familiar Git platform conventions: tabs with counters, a branch selector, Watch/Star/Fork, and a 'Go to file' search with a keyboard shortcut.
The layout is clean, with clear grouping of repo stats, toolbar, files, README and metadata sidebar.

recommendations.recommendation: Raise the contrast of secondary text (commit messages, timestamps, placeholders, 'Manage Topics') and of control borders in the dark theme, so they meet WCAG 1.4.3 (4.5:1) and 1.4.11 (3:1).
Replace the ambiguous 'Escape' button in the README header with a descriptive label such as 'Show escaped characters', or add a tooltip or notice explaining why it appears.
Show absolute timestamps next to, or on hover over, relative times like 'now' in the latest commit bar, so users can confirm exactly when the latest commit happened.
Narrow the gap between file names and commit messages, or add row hover highlighting, to strengthen the visual link within each file row.
Remove the duplicate Stars/Watchers/Forks counts from the sidebar (they are already in the header buttons), and consider hiding the page render timings from the footer for non-admin users.

Icons are used the same way in the tabs and sidebar. Some labels use title case ('Pull Requests', 'Add File') and others use sentence case ('Go to file', 'Manage Topics' vs 'Search code...').
dimensions.justification: The page is very consistent with Git platform standards and within itself. Only small inconsistencies in label case.

dimensions.evidence: The 'Code' tab is underlined as active. The breadcrumb shows judge-demo / web-shop, the branch selector shows 'main', and the Issues tab shows a counter of 4. Watching 1, Star 0 and Fork 0 have counters. Every commit time reads 'now'.

dimensions.justification: A read-only overview has little risk of error, and the potentially risky areas are tucked away. There isn't much else on this page to judge.

dimensions.evidence: The latest commit message, hash and time show at the top of the file list without any clicks. The 'docs' folder row reads 'Add docs/INSTALL.md'. 'Go to file' has a T keyboard shortcut and 'Search code...' has an S shortcut.
dimensions.justification: The task takes at most 1–2 clicks (docs → INSTALL.md, or Go to file). The latest commit can be checked right away, and keyboard shortcuts are shown.

dimensions.evidence: The dark interface is uncluttered. The sidebar shows a short set of stats (26 KiB, 0 Stars, 1 Watchers, 0 Forks). The footer shows technical render times (Page: 13ms Template: 3ms). The Stars/Watchers/Forks stats repeat the counters in the header buttons.
dimensions.justification: The page is generally lean. The repeated counters and developer-oriented footer metrics add small amounts of noise.

dimensions.evidence: The theme is dark. Secondary text such as the commit messages in the file list, the 'now' timestamps, the 'Go to file' placeholder and the footer is mid-grey on a dark grey background. Counter badges (1, 0, 4) are small and low-contrast. The blue folder icons and links depend partly on colour. The compare and RSS icon buttons have no text.
dimensions.justification: Main text is readable, but several secondary elements look close to or below the 4.5:1 contrast ratio, and the small badges and icon-only controls are harder for low-vision users. Fix: raise the contrast of muted text and badges, and add visible labels or tooltips to icon-only buttons. Focus states can't be judged from a static screenshot.

strengths: The latest commit (author, hash, message, time) is shown at the top of the file list, so you can check it without clicking.
The layout follows Git platform conventions: tabs, branch selector, Watch/Star/Fork and the Code clone button are all where users expect them.
Go to file (T) and Search code (S) are fast ways to find a file and show their keyboard shortcuts.

recommendations.recommendation: Raise the contrast of muted grey text (commit messages, timestamps, placeholders, counter badges) to at least 4.5:1 on the dark background.
Rename the 'Escape' button in the README header to something descriptive like 'Show hidden characters', or add an explanatory tooltip.
Add a visible label or tooltip to the icon-only compare button next to the branch selector and to the RSS button.
Show the absolute date next to relative times like 'now', or on hover, so the time of the latest commit can be checked precisely.
Remove the Stars/Watchers/Forks stats from the sidebar, since the header buttons already show those counts, and hide the render-time metrics in the footer for normal users.
